headline: No on-chain admin or upgrade path; changes require broad off-chain social consensus among core devs, node operators, and validators
short_headline: Off-chain social consensus, immutable deposit contract

findings.text: Beacon Deposit Contract (0x00000000219ab540356cBB839Cbe05303d7705Fa) has no owner, admin, pendingOwner, governor, or pause methods (Etherscan Read Contract tab and verified ABI show only get_deposit_count, get_deposit_root, supportsInterface, deposit).

Deposit contract is immutable (non-proxy, no upgrade functions; verified exact match on Etherscan). Core protocol has no smart-contract upgrade surface; governance is entirely off-chain via EIPs and client implementations.

No on-chain execution path, timelock, or queue exists for protocol changes. Execution path is off-chain: EIP proposal → ACD calls / Ethereum Magicians discussion → rough consensus → client implementation → node operator / validator adoption (https://ethereum.org/governance/).
No multisigs with reachable control over core protocol or deposit contract. No Security Council or emergency multisig identified on-chain or in governance docs.
No on-chain Governor, voting token, proposal threshold, or quorum. Governance is off-chain social consensus; no numeric constants readable via on-chain calls.
No emergency pause, guardian role, or time-capped emergency powers documented for core protocol or deposit contract.

Highest reachable tier on uncontested path is T3 (governance-internal rule changes via EIP process) or T4 (operational client coordination). T1 (fund-critical: mint/drain/replace implementation on user funds) and T2 unreachable because deposit contract is immutable and core protocol has no admin-controlled functions.

steelman.red: Off-chain process could theoretically be captured by a small set of core devs or Ethereum Foundation influence, allowing rapid rule changes without on-chain delay or user exit window.
steelman.orange: Lack of formal on-chain timelock or multisig threshold leaves upgrade path dependent on informal social consensus that could be faster or slower than 7 days depending on coordination.
steelman.green: No single EOA, 2-of-3 multisig, or governance contract can unilaterally perform T1 or T2 actions; deposit contract is immutable with no admin path, and core changes require broad validator adoption, satisfying green criteria for T3/T4 with no timelock needed.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the evidence shows T1/T2 actions are unreachable on-chain (immutable deposit contract with no owner/admin) and core governance is off-chain social consensus requiring broad adoption, which aligns with the green steel-man for T3/T4 paths regardless of timelock (C1–C7 from Etherscan deposit contract page and ethereum.org/governance/).

evidence.shows: Contract overview, verification status (Exact Match), Read Contract methods (no owner/admin/paused/governor), ABI, and immutable nature of Beacon Deposit Contract.

Explicit statement that Ethereum governance is off-chain; details EIP process, AllCoreDevs calls, rough consensus, no on-chain voting or governance tokens, no mention of timelocks/multisigs/admin controls/emergency powers.
Canonical execution client repository with open-source governance via PRs and community discussion; no on-chain control references.

unknowns: C3: exact on-chain execution path and numeric delay constants unavailable because no on-chain governance contracts exist to query via /api/contract/read or Etherscan Read Contract for this protocol slice.
C4: no multisig addresses surfaced from pinned sources or deposit contract; any potential off-chain coordination groups not enumerated in fetched governance page.

Governance occurs entirely off-chain through EIPs, All Core Devs calls, and rough community consensus with no central admin, timelock, or on-chain voting token.

headline: Permissionless on-chain exits and transactions; no admin-controlled pause on claims or requests; immutable deposit contract
short_headline: Fully permissionless exit, no admin pause

findings.text: User-facing exit functions: deposit() (entry), and on beacon chain side: voluntary exit, withdrawal request/claim processes (no single 'withdraw' in deposit contract; staking exits handled via consensus layer).

Deposit contract deposit() is permissionless (payable, no modifiers). No pause guards or access controls on any functions (Etherscan ABI shows no onlyRole/whenNotPaused). Beacon chain exits are permissionless for validator operators.
No pause guards, PAUSE_ROLE, GUARDIAN, or paused() method on deposit contract. No actor can call indefinite or time-capped pause.
No emergency vs governance pause distinction; no pause functionality exists at all for the deposit contract or core transaction layer.
Staking withdrawal queue exists on beacon chain with documented processing (not indefinite; bounded by protocol rules), but not pausable by any admin.
Permissionless emergency exit via standard transaction submission or validator exit; no forced-exit needed because no admin freeze capability exists.
All core functions (send ETH, deploy contracts, stake via deposit, exit validators) are directly callable on-chain via any wallet/RPC without official frontend.

steelman.red: Staking withdrawals have a queue that could theoretically delay exits under extreme network conditions, and off-chain social consensus could influence future exit rules without on-chain cap.
steelman.orange: Withdrawal queue duration can exceed 7 days in high-demand periods, and no formal on-chain time cap on processing is readable in the deposit contract itself.
steelman.green: No admin (EOA, multisig, or governance) can pause claims of finalized exits or new requests; deposit contract is immutable with no pause path, and all user actions (including staking exit) are permissionless on-chain with no frontend dependency for core functionality.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because E1–E7 evidence shows fully permissionless on-chain exit paths with zero admin pause capability on the immutable deposit contract and core transaction layer (Etherscan deposit contract page), satisfying all green criteria even with beacon chain queue mechanics.

evidence.shows: Verified ABI with only permissionless deposit() function; no pause, owner, or access control methods present; contract holds user-staked ETH but exposes no admin-gated exit controls.
Confirms no on-chain admin controls or pause mechanisms for user funds or protocol rules.

unknowns: E5: exact maximum queue duration and pausability of beacon chain withdrawal queue not re-read on-chain in this run (corroboration from governance page only; no direct /api/contract/read on consensus layer contracts performed).

headline: Highly autonomous base layer; validator set diversified with no single external dependency able to cause principal loss or freeze
short_headline: Decentralized validators, no critical external deps

findings.text: Core contracts (deposit contract) call no external oracles, price feeds, or third-party contracts; only internal beacon chain logic. No getPrice/latestAnswer calls.

Validator set is permissionless and highly diversified (tens of thousands of independent operators); no small committee or single operator set controls consensus or can cause >5% principal loss via coordinated failure (substrate property, not external dep).
No bridge/cross-chain dependencies for core L1 operation or user principal; staking is L1-native.
No nested collateral/restaking chains in core protocol; deposit contract accepts plain ETH only.
No forkedFrom lineage recorded in DeFiLlama context or fetched sources.
Fallbacks: diversified validator set and client diversity act as live circuit breakers; no single point of failure for consensus or fund custody.
Not an appchain; inherits Ethereum L1 substrate (no additional sequencer/DA dependency).
No keeper/relayer dependency for core user actions; permissionless transaction submission and validator operation.
No governance-mutable external dependency surface; immutable deposit contract and off-chain governance cannot silently introduce new trusted contracts that affect user principal.

steelman.red: Validator set or client diversity failure could theoretically degrade performance or delay exits, and off-chain social consensus could introduce changes affecting expected staking yield.
steelman.orange: Staking participants depend on validator liveness and client implementations for yield and exit finality; a coordinated but non-malicious failure could freeze withdrawals temporarily.
steelman.green: No external dependency (oracle, bridge, small operator set, or mutable governance surface) can cause loss of user principal or unclaimed yield; all critical paths are diversified on-chain or substrate-level with live mitigations (A1–A9).

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because A1–A9 findings confirm no material external dependencies capable of principal loss (validator set is substrate, not external; deposit contract has zero external calls), with impacted TVS effectively 0% under any single dependency failure.

evidence.shows: ABI contains no external contract calls, oracles, or dependencies; only internal deposit logic.
Emphasizes decentralized validator and node operator participation with no single point of control or external dependency for protocol operation.
Open client implementation supporting permissionless node operation; no external deps listed for core consensus.

unknowns: A2: precise current validator count and diversification metrics not re-queried on-chain in this run (governance page corroboration only).

headline: Fully permissionless on-chain access; no whitelist, KYC, or operator approval required; multiple independent paths exist

findings.text: No whitelist/allowlist/onlyWhitelisted/isKYCed modifiers on any user-facing functions in deposit contract or core protocol (ABI and Etherscan confirm permissionless deposit and transaction layer).
No off-chain operators, keepers, or privileged relayers required to admit user actions; transaction submission and staking are unconditional and permissionless.
Official frontend (ethereum.org) has standard ToS with jurisdictional language (A3-passive); no active IP geo-blocking or wallet screening enforced on-chain. Reported as context only.

Independent access paths exist: published SDKs (ethers.js, web3.js), third-party frontends (Etherscan write tab, Rabby, MetaMask), wallet integrations, DEX/aggregator routing, and direct RPC calls to any node.
No on-chain sanctions blocklist or OFAC-style address checks in deposit contract or core protocol.
Read access fully permissionless (anyone can query state via RPC); write access also permissionless for all core functions.

ToS on ethereum.org contains standard eligibility language (e.g., comply with applicable law, restricted territories self-certification); verbatim extraction limited by page render but context confirms no contract-level enforcement.

steelman.red: Official frontend ToS includes jurisdictional restrictions and potential future compliance tooling could gate access for some users.
steelman.orange: Heavy reliance on official resources for discovery, though contracts remain open; no single published SDK is mandated but practical UX often routes through known tools.
steelman.green: Contracts admit all users unconditionally with no whitelist/KYC/operator approval; at least one (actually many) independent A3b paths exist (SDKs, wallets, third-party UIs, direct RPC), satisfying green criteria regardless of frontend ToS posture.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because A1–A6 evidence confirms fully permissionless on-chain admission with no contract-level gates and multiple independent access paths (Etherscan deposit contract ABI + ethereum.org/governance confirming decentralized nature), defaulting to green per guidelines.

evidence.shows: ABI and contract page confirm no access control modifiers, whitelist functions, or on-chain blocklists; all entry points permissionless.
Describes permissionless participation by anyone (ETH holders, node operators, developers) with no admission gates or KYC requirements at protocol level.
Open client and tooling enabling independent access via any RPC or SDK without official frontend cooperation.

unknowns: A6: verbatim ToS jurisdictional clause extraction failed due to page render limits on ethereum.org; recorded as context only.

headline: Core contracts and clients fully verified and open-source with public specs and formal verification history
short_headline: Verified bytecode, open-source clients, audited specs

findings.text: Beacon Deposit Contract bytecode is Source Code Verified (Exact Match) on Etherscan with full ABI and source available; not a proxy.
Source corresponds to public consensus-specs repository (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs); deposit contract source matches verified Etherscan code at pinned commit in specs history.

Deposit contract covered by formal verification audit from Runtime Verification (2020) and additional analyses; core client implementations (go-ethereum) have extensive community and professional review.
Runtime Verification is a recognized firm for formal verification; multiple other recognized auditors have reviewed Ethereum clients and specs historically.
No post-audit drift on deposit contract (immutable and matches audited spec commit); core clients evolve via public PRs with ongoing review.
Deposit contract is not proxied; implementation is the verified contract itself. Core protocol clients are source-available, not smart-contract proxies.

steelman.red: Core protocol evolves rapidly via client releases; without a single 'current deployment commit' for the entire chain, full end-to-end bytecode equivalence for every client is hard to assert at any snapshot.
steelman.orange: Some peripheral tooling or older audits may show minor drift, and formal verification was scoped to deposit contract only, not the full live chain state.
steelman.green: Deposit contract is exactly verified on Etherscan matching public source repo at known commit; core clients are open-source with public specs and recognized formal verification; no unverified critical contracts.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because V1–V6 evidence from Etherscan (exact match verification) and GitHub consensus-specs/repo shows full source correspondence and audit coverage for the key on-chain component, with client verifiability via public repos satisfying all green criteria.

evidence.shows: Source Code Verified (Exact Match), compiler v0.6.11, full source/ABI available, Swarm source IPFS link, no proxy.
Official source for deposit contract matching Etherscan verified code (per eth2book.info and Runtime Verification reports).
Canonical open-source execution client with full source, SECURITY.md, and community-verified builds.
Formal verification report by recognized firm Runtime Verification covering deposit contract bytecode correctness against spec.

unknowns: V2: exact commit SHA for live client deployments not pinned in this run (repo-level evidence only; bytecode diff not performed).
